# Signal Messenger `libsignal`

The crates in this directory compile and wrap code of Signal's `libsignal`, so that the generated
AArch64 machine code can be verified in Lean. This file records what comes from
`libsignal`, from where, and under which license.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Project | [`signalapp/libsignal`](https://github.com/signalapp/libsignal) |
| Version | tag `v0.105.4`, commit `b2a5c30f3245c1bcad04b27b1e752a38321c793d` |
| Copyright | Copyright 2020-2026 Signal Messenger, LLC. |
| License | `AGPL-3.0-only`; full text in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE), copied from the upstream `LICENSE` at that commit |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No upstream checkout and no compiler output is committed in this repository.** Every
> `libsignal-*/vendor/` (a symlink to a libsignal checkout), every `target/` and `.GeneratedLean/`
> (the AArch64 machine code compiled from these crates and the upstream sources) are gitignored
> build products, regenerated locally by `lake build`. The libsignal material that *is* committed
> is listed item by item below.

## Crates

| Directory | What it is | Copied upstream code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`libsignal-session/`](libsignal-session) | wrappers and the `libsignal-cli` CLI around the 1:1 session API (`src/`, `cli/`), plus untrusted tooling (`tools/`, `tests/`) | none in the wrappers; see item 2 for `tools/` |
| [`bug-injection/`](bug-injection) | known, upstream-fixed libsignal bugs as patches, with the registry, witness inputs and replayer of the bug-injection framework (`Symbolic/BugInjection/README.md`); not part of any image | the patches: see item 3 |
| [`test-vectors/`](test-vectors) | Lean data module (`lean_lib LibsignalTestVectors`) holding test vectors of libsignal's own tests, imported by Lean tests under `Computational/Tests/` | the vectors: see item 4 |

Each file states its license in its header comment: portions copied from `libsignal` keep Signal
Messenger's copyright and `SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only`, and the Google-authored code
is `Copyright 2026 Google LLC` under `Apache-2.0`. Files without a header comment (the
`Cargo.toml`, `translation.toml`, `events.toml` and `cli-elf/` `.toml`/`.lock`/`.ld` configuration files
and the `README.md` files) are Google-authored. A few files in `libsignal-session/cli-elf/` contain
code from other projects and say so in their header: `rdl_shim.S` and `stock/rdl_shim.S` (Rust standard library 1.98.1,
`Copyright (c) The Rust Project Contributors`, `MIT OR Apache-2.0`), `string-include/features.h`
and `string-include/string.h` (musl 1.2.5, `Copyright © 2005-2020 Rich Felker, et al.`, `MIT`),
and the generated `signal_session_io.S`, which is compiled from the Google-authored `cli/io` crate
and contains inlined Rust `core`/`alloc` code (`MIT OR Apache-2.0`). The `Cargo.lock` files are generated by Cargo; they name upstream crate
versions and checksums and contain no upstream code.

The headers of the verified crate (`libsignal-session` incl. `cli/`) must keep their
line counts: the source line of every panic site is compiled into the verified machine code.

## Build-time dependency and generated machine code

`libsignal-session` depends on libsignal v0.105.4 (`b2a5c30`) through path dependencies on
`vendor/libsignal`, a gitignored symlink to a libsignal checkout that `rust-obj2lean` resolves or
fetches at build time (`[upstream]` in the crate's `translation.toml`: `$LIBSIGNAL_SRC`,
`~/sw/libsignal`, or a shallow clone of tag `v0.105.4`).

The AArch64 machine code that `lake build` generates from `libsignal-session/translation.toml` into
the gitignored `.GeneratedLean/GeneratedLean/` (every `Libsignal*` file: `LibsignalSessionObj`,
`LibsignalSessionPlacedObj`, `LibsignalSessionCode`, `LibsignalSession*`, `LibsignalTripleRatchet*`)
is compiled from AGPL-3.0-only source and is a derived work of libsignal; the separately translated
I/O crate `libsignal-session/cli/io/translation.toml` (`SignalSessionIoObj`,
`SignalSessionIoPlacedObj`, `SignalSessionIoCode`) is compiled from original Google-authored
`Apache-2.0` code (`libsignal-session/cli/io/src/lib.rs`, plus inlined Rust `core`/`alloc` and `std`
re-exports of `core`/`alloc` items under `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, with no `std::fs`/`std::io`) and copies no upstream `libsignal` source. Each generated `*Obj` /
`*PlacedObj` module carries the `license_header` of its `translation.toml`.

## libsignal-derived material committed in this repository

1. **[`libsignal-session/src/lib.rs`](libsignal-session/src/lib.rs)** and
   **[`libsignal-session/cli/src/`](libsignal-session/cli/src)**: wrappers and CLI entry points that call libsignal's public
   API (`message_encrypt`, `message_decrypt_signal`, `process_prekey_bundle`,
   `SignalMessage::try_from`, the in-memory stores); the companion CLI process-I/O crate
   **[`libsignal-session/cli/io/src/lib.rs`](libsignal-session/cli/io/src/lib.rs)** uses bounded C-ABI `musl` syscalls (`open`, `read`, `write`, `close`, `__errno_location`; no `std::fs`/`std::io`; only `std` re-exports of `core` items and `alloc::vec::Vec`) with no `libsignal` dependency. None of them copies upstream source.

2. **[`libsignal-session/tools/prost-diff/src/main.rs`](libsignal-session/tools/prost-diff/src/main.rs)**
   (untrusted differential-fuzz tool): `SignalMessage` (lines 30-44) is prost-build's output for
   upstream `rust/protocol/src/proto/wire.proto` (`Copyright 2020 Signal Messenger, LLC.`).

3. **[`bug-injection/patches/`](bug-injection/patches)** (inputs of the bug-injection framework,
   `Symbolic/BugInjection/README.md`; never compiled into a verified image): each directory holds
   the diff of an upstream libsignal fix commit, byte-identical to
   `https://github.com/signalapp/libsignal/commit/<sha>.diff` (`upstream-<sha>.diff`), and that
   diff's reversal ported to v0.105.4 (`v0.105.4.diff`, with a preamble saying so). Both contain
   libsignal source lines (`Copyright 2020-2026 Signal Messenger, LLC.`, `AGPL-3.0-only`, full
   text in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)). The fix commits are
   `5293caa6cad81566b80f3c3731857bedaa78737b` and `cd361186fba60c83186262d91b03af608fb8c7c3`
   (listed in `bug-injection/bugs.toml`). The replayer, registry, witness inputs and README beside
   them are Google-authored.

4. **[`test-vectors/LibsignalTestVectors/ChainKeyDerivation.lean`](test-vectors/LibsignalTestVectors/ChainKeyDerivation.lean)**
   (Lean module `LibsignalTestVectors.ChainKeyDerivation`, library `LibsignalTestVectors` in
   `lakefile.lean`): the four 32-byte vectors `seed`, `message_key`, `mac_key` and
   `next_chain_key` of libsignal's own test `test_chain_key_derivation`
   (`rust/protocol/src/ratchet/keys.rs:231-277`, `Copyright 2020 Signal Messenger, LLC.`,
   `AGPL-3.0-only`, full text in [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)), as hex literals; the file holds nothing
   else. The Lean tests
   [`Computational/Tests/AEAD/HKDFTest.lean`](../../Computational/Tests/AEAD/HKDFTest.lean) and
   [`Computational/Tests/Binary/SessionRunTest.lean`](../../Computational/Tests/Binary/SessionRunTest.lean)
   import it and contain no copy of the vectors.

Elsewhere, Lean files and Markdown cite libsignal by file and line and describe its behaviour in
prose or pseudocode; they do not copy its source.
